skill.name: marketing-ideas
skill.description: Select, score, and prioritize SaaS marketing ideas using a structured Marketing Feasibility Score.
skill.summary: Prioritize SaaS marketing ideas with feasibility scoring and execution guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline score formatting, not executable Ruby or shell code. The system reconnaissance finding is also a false positive because the cited line discusses paid acquisition as a growth channel. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unsafe execution behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown code fences and inline backticks triggered external command heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Keep formulas in plain Markdown or label code fences as text to reduce future scanner noise.

static_findings.snippet: * Favor: paid acquisition, partnerships, PLG loops

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 80-83 contain a Markdown code fence showing the Marketing Feasibility Score formula. There is no Ruby code, shell command, or execution instruction.
The cited content closes the Markdown formula block and continues with score range text. It is documentation formatting, not backtick command execution.
Line 85 uses inline Markdown backticks around a score range. The surrounding section explains marketing scoring and contains no executable command context.
Lines 113-115 contain a Markdown code fence with an arithmetic scoring example. It is static documentation and cannot execute shell or Ruby commands.
The cited block is the end of a Markdown example and a written interpretation of the score. No command invocation, interpreter directive, or user-controlled execution is present.
Line 189 says to favor paid acquisition, partnerships, and product-led growth loops for growth-stage SaaS. This is marketing guidance, not system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: SaaS teams often have too many growth ideas and limited time. This skill filters ideas, scores feasibility, and turns the best options into clear next steps.
actual_capabilities: Asks for product, audience, stage, budget, team, and goal before recommending tactics.
Shortlists relevant SaaS marketing ideas based on business constraints.
Scores each idea with impact, effort, cost, speed, and fit dimensions.
Recommends only the top three to five ideas with positive feasibility scores.
Provides first steps, success metrics, expected outcomes, resources, and execution risks.
limitations: It does not run campaigns, buy media, or connect to marketing platforms.
It depends on accurate user context for useful scoring.
It cannot verify live market data or competitor performance without external research.
The referenced 140 idea library is summarized in this file rather than fully included.

use_cases.title: Choose early traction channels
use_cases.description: Rank low-cost marketing tests for a new SaaS product with a small team and short feedback window.

use_cases.title: Focus a growth roadmap
use_cases.description: Compare acquisition, partnership, SEO, and product-led ideas before committing quarterly marketing resources.

use_cases.title: Prepare client recommendations
use_cases.description: Turn a broad list of marketing options into scored, defensible priorities for a SaaS client.

prompt_templates.title: Score my SaaS ideas
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to score marketing ideas for my SaaS. Product: [product]. ICP: [audience]. Stage: [stage]. Budget: [budget]. Team: [team]. Goal: [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Find the best first tests
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an early-stage SaaS with limited budget. Ask any missing context, then recommend the top three high-signal marketing tests using MFS.

prompt_templates.title: Compare channel options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare SEO, paid acquisition, partnerships, founder-led content, and PLG loops for this SaaS: [details]. Score each option and explain which to delay.

prompt_templates.title: Build a staged growth plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-day marketing plan from the highest-scoring ideas. Include MFS, sequencing, first steps, success metrics, resources, and execution risks.

output_examples.input: Early-stage B2B analytics SaaS, two-person team, small budget, goal is qualified leads.
output: Top recommendation: comparison pages with a strong fit score because buyers already search for alternatives.
Second recommendation: founder-led LinkedIn content because cost is low and learning speed is high.
Deferred: paid acquisition because budget limits meaningful testing.

output_examples.input: Growth-stage product-led SaaS with active users and a goal to increase expansion revenue.
output: Top recommendation: in-product upgrade prompts tied to usage milestones.
Second recommendation: lifecycle email campaigns based on feature adoption.
Primary risk: weak event tracking will make attribution and iteration difficult.

best_practices: Provide product stage, audience, budget, team capacity, and primary goal before asking for recommendations.
Use the MFS score to compare options, then validate the top ideas with small tests.
Review risks and resource needs before adding any idea to a roadmap.
anti_patterns: Asking for a long list of generic marketing ideas without business context.
Choosing novelty over fit, learning speed, or execution capacity.
Treating scores as final truth instead of planning assumptions to test.

faq.question: What is the Marketing Feasibility Score?
faq.answer: It scores impact, fit, speed, effort, and cost to compare marketing ideas for a specific SaaS context.

faq.question: Can this skill create a full campaign plan?
faq.answer: It can outline first steps, metrics, resources, and risks for selected ideas. It does not execute campaigns.

faq.question: Does it work only for SaaS products?
faq.answer: The guidance is written for SaaS and software products. Other businesses may need adapted scoring assumptions.

faq.question: How many ideas will it recommend?
faq.answer: The skill is designed to recommend no more than five ideas and to avoid ideas with poor feasibility.

faq.question: Can it use live competitor data?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Provide research or ask the host assistant to gather current data before scoring.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
